Healthy diet

26 January 2026
Share on Facebook

Key facts

  • Diet plays a critical role in shaping the health and well-being of both individuals and populations.
  • A diet must also be safe to be healthy, i.e. free from microbial and chemical contaminants.

WHO guidance on healthy diets

Sugars

  • The consumption of free sugars should be limited to less than 10% of total daily energy intake, which is equivalent to 50 g (or about 12 level teaspoons) for a person of healthy body weight consuming about 2000 calories per day.
  • Consumption of free sugars should be limited throughout the life course.

Salt/sodium and potassium

Sodium and potassium are essential minerals but high intake of sodium (salt) is associated with increased blood pressure.

  • In adults, salt intake should be limited to less than 5 grams per day (2 grams per day sodium).

How to promote healthy diets

  • encouraging consumer demand for healthy foods and meals through:
    • promoting consumer awareness of a healthy diet;
    • encouraging culinary skills, including in children through schools;
